s3-key-decode.why: The ingest handler uses `name = unquote_plus(rec["object"]["key"])` before filtering and scheduling.

two-hour-hold.why: The ingest handler creates an EventBridge Scheduler one-time schedule `at(now + HOLD)` with HOLD = 2 hours.

stale-generation.why: The S3 versionId is passed as `generation`, and transcode compares `head.get("VersionId")` with `job["generation"]`, returning stale on mismatch or 404; versioning is enabled on the bucket.

overwrite-trigger.why: `aws_s3_bucket_notification` uses `events = ["s3:ObjectCreated:*"]`, which fires on overwrites too.

transcode-timeout.why: Lambda timeout is set to 900, and summary item 1 explicitly flags the 15-minute limit and suggests Fargate or Batch.

rate-limit.why: Summary item 5 explicitly says the 5/s and 3-concurrent limits are not enforced and explains why reserved concurrency was not set.

retry-policy.why: Ingest gets `maximum_retry_attempts = 0`, and summary item 4 explicitly flags that the Cloud Tasks backoff has no equivalent, describing the new 3 schedule plus 2 Lambda retries.

attribute-limit.why: The 12 attributes are moved into a JSON SNS message body, and this is flagged in summary item 9.

week-start.why: `date_trunc('week', CAST(uploaded_at AS date) + INTERVAL '1' DAY) - INTERVAL '1' DAY` correctly produces Sunday-start weeks.

weekend-days.why: Uses `COUNT_IF(day_of_week(uploaded_at) IN (6, 7))`, with a comment on Trino's Monday=1 numbering.

safe-divide.why: `CAST(SUM(transcode_seconds) AS double) / COUNT(*)` avoids integer truncation, and COUNT(*) per group is always at least 1, as noted in summary item 15.

no-silent-changes.why: 7-day retention (SQS) and 4096 MB memory are preserved, and versioning, region, retries, auth, event format and timeout changes are all called out; the only unflagged item is the broad `scheduler:CreateSchedule` on `*`, a necessary new grant rather than a behaviour change.
